title: Cap. III open + Rat. 1: common inefficacious will before foresight of merits
pass_a_gloss:
Chapter III. The adversaries' arguments are weighed and dissolved.

Now let us ventilate the adversaries' reasons. First, therefore, they try to demonstrate that no one is elected to glory by an efficacious will of God except from foreseen merits, by this kind of argumentation:

Reason 1. The will of giving eternal life which precedes the foresight of merits is a certain common and inefficacious will, which regards all men equally, both the reprobate and the predestinate: Therefore, that God efficaciously wills to give glory to someone depends on the foresight of merits.
pass_b_english:
Cap. III — the adversaries' arguments weighed and answered.

Now to their reasons. First they try to prove no one is chosen for glory by God's efficacious will except from foreseen merits, like this:

Rat. 1. The will to give eternal life that comes before foresight of merits is only a common, inefficacious will, looking equally at all — reprobate and predestinate alike. So if God efficaciously wills glory for someone, that hangs on foresight of merits.
source_text:
CAP. III. Argumenta adversariorum expenduntur & dissolvuntur.

Jam rationes adversariorum ventilemus. Primo igitur conantur demonstrare, neminem esse efficaci Dei voluntate electum ad gloriam nisi ex meritis praevisis, hujusmodi argumentatione:

Rat. 1. Voluntas dandi vitam aeternam, quae antecedit praevisionem meritorum, est quaedam voluntas communis & inefficax, quae ex aequo respicit omnes homines, tam praeteritos quam praedestinatos: Ergo quod vult Deus alicui efficaciter dare gloriam, pendet ex praevisione meritorum.
